A1.justification: Both PDFs describe UniVideo and contain readable methods, results, figures, tables, and appendices. Added material and relocated sections can be reliably matched.

before.justification: v3 reports original video generation and editing evaluations, human assessments, architectural ablations, and qualitative generalization results.

after.justification: v4 retains those original experiments and adds image generation and editing evaluations, a prompt-rewriting comparison, and detailed VBench results.

M1.justification: The dual-stream architecture, connector, visual conditioning, and three training stages remain unchanged. 'Generation with thinking' renames the existing visual-prompt procedure. Expanded data-construction descriptions do not establish a change to the underlying method.

E1.justification: v4 adds evaluation on GenEval, ImgEdit-Bench, and GEdit-Bench-EN, substantially extending evaluated coverage to image generation and editing. These tasks were already included in training; existing video and understanding coverage is retained.

E2.justification: New image comparisons include SDXL and FLUX.1-dev on GenEval and GPT-4o and Step1X-Edit on image editing. The detailed VBench comparison adds participants such as TUNA and MiniMax-Video-01. Existing in-context comparison sets remain unchanged.

E3.justification: The added image evaluations introduce benchmark-specific scoring and GenEval conditions with and without an LLM prompt rewriter. Existing training hyperparameters and the 20-case in-context benchmark remain unchanged. v4 newly identifies GPT-enhanced VBench prompts, without establishing that v3 used different prompts.

E4.justification: v4 Table 2 adds a prompt-rewriting comparison, reporting GenEval overall scores of 0.53 without rewriting and 0.69 with it. Existing connector, multi-task, visual-input, and zero-shot analyses are retained despite relocation and table merging.

E5.justification: Both versions specify at least three annotators per human-rated sample. Neither reports experimental seed counts, repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals, or significance tests; v4 does not introduce such reporting.

E6.justification: v4 adds substantial image benchmark results, including ImgEdit-Bench overall 3.83, and detailed VBench scores. UniVideo's reported VBench total changes from 82.58 in v3 Table 2 to 83.48 in v4 Table 1, without establishing identical evaluation conditions. Existing in-context and ablation scores are retained.

T1.justification: Appendix G.1 newly defines a visibility consistency score as the fraction of track frames whose mask area exceeds a threshold, together with a rejection rule. v3 described filtering only generally. No theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: The abstract and first contribution explicitly extend performance and unification claims to image generation and editing. The central architecture and generalization claims remain; 'generation with thinking' reframes the existing visual-prompt capability.

C2.justification: v4 interprets image performance despite limited Stage 3 text-to-image sampling and explains why gray-tile conditioning supports stylized-to-real transfer from real-to-real training. Existing limitations concerning over-editing, motion preservation, and free-form editing success remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendix G substantially expands data-construction documentation: detector and MLLM roles, object-area thresholds, 1B auxiliary models, VIVID-10M, 10K reconstruction pairs, filtering instructions, and approximately 500K image-editing samples. These are newly disclosed details, not established retraining. v4 also drops the explicit statement that reported results default to the hidden-state variant.

R1.justification: v4 adds citations including GenEval, VIVID-10M, Grounding DINO, TUNA, ReCamMaster, and Movie Weaver. Research positioning remains substantially intact; most extended related-work discussion is relocated from Section 4 to Appendix C.

P1.justification: v4 substantially reorganizes the narrative by moving model-design analysis and detailed related work into appendices, expanding data-construction explanations, and inserting image-evaluation subsections. It also renames visual-prompt sections and adds an LLM-use statement.

P2.justification: v4 adds three result tables and two data-construction/filtering figures, expands the overview figure with image examples, and redraws conditioning diagrams. It merges the two ablation tables, places single- and multi-reference results side by side, and relocates multiple existing displays.

improvement.justification: The added image evaluations, explicit prompt-rewriting comparison, and detailed data-construction appendix improve empirical support and transparency. The central video evidence and qualitative generalization demonstrations remain largely unchanged. The unexplained VBench score update does not establish a same-setting performance improvement, limiting the additional conclusions supported by the revision.
